title: What is RAM?
answer: RAM is your computer’s short-term working memory. It holds the information your apps are using right now. Storage keeps your files when the power is off; RAM does not.
sections: Think of it as your workbench

Your storage is the cupboard where you keep everything. RAM is the workbench where you spread out the things you are using. A bigger workbench lets you work on more things at once, but it does not make every individual tool faster.
What happens when memory fills up?

Your operating system can move less-active data to storage to free up RAM. This is slower than accessing RAM directly. Switching between apps may feel sluggish, especially when several demanding programs are open. A slow computer can have other causes, so check memory use before buying an upgrade.
Check before you upgrade

On Windows, open Task Manager and choose Performance, then Memory. On macOS, open Activity Monitor and look at Memory Pressure. Check this while doing your usual work. Consult your device manual before buying: some memory is soldered in place, and different DDR generations are not interchangeable.
Does more RAM mean more storage?
No. Adding RAM does not give you more room for saved photos or games. You need more storage for that. The right memory capacity depends on the apps you use and their requirements.
author: Tech Compass

title: Wi-Fi connected. Internet missing?
keywords: fix wifi wi fi wireless internet offline laptop cant get online disconnecting network router
answer: First check whether the problem affects one device or every device. That tells you whether to start with your computer or your network. Try the steps below in order and test after each one.
sections: 1. Check the basics
Make sure Wi-Fi is on and airplane mode is off. Confirm you joined your own network. Open a second website: if only one site fails, your connection may be working.
2. Try another device

Connect a phone to the same Wi-Fi and temporarily turn off mobile data. If it also cannot get online, check your provider’s outage page using mobile data. If only your computer fails, concentrate on that computer.
3. Reconnect and restart

Turn Wi-Fi off and back on. Save your work and restart the affected device. If multiple devices fail, restart the router using its power switch or manufacturer instructions. This temporarily disconnects everyone; do not press the factory-reset button.
4. Check device settings

On Windows, use Settings → Network & internet and the network troubleshooter in Get Help. On a Mac, check System Settings → Wi-Fi and the network recommendations if shown. Move closer to the router to test whether distance or interference is involved.
5. Get specific help

If the problem continues, record the error message, affected devices, and whether the network appears. Contact your internet provider for a whole-network failure or your device support team for a device-only failure. Avoid a network reset until you understand which saved network and VPN settings it removes.
author: Tech Compass

title: Why is my computer running slowly?
keywords: slow laptop lag freezing performance startup computer
answer: A slow computer may be short of memory or storage space, busy with background work, or getting too hot. Start by finding what is busy instead of installing a cleaner app.
sections: 1. Restart, then observe
Save your work and restart. Open only the app you need. Note whether the slowdown starts immediately, after opening a particular app, or after the computer has been running for a while.
2. Look for the bottleneck

In Windows Task Manager or macOS Activity Monitor, inspect CPU and memory usage. A high number during a demanding task is normal. A program that stays busy when you are doing nothing deserves a closer look. Do not end unfamiliar system processes.
3. Make room and reduce startup work

Review your Downloads folder and uninstall apps you no longer use through system settings. Back up files before removing them. Review startup or login items and disable optional apps you recognize. Do not delete system folders.
4. Check updates and airflow

Install supported operating-system and app updates. Keep ventilation openings clear and use a laptop on a hard surface. If the device is unusually hot, shuts itself down, or has a swollen battery, stop using it and seek qualified service.
When to consider an upgrade

Measure first. Consistently high memory pressure may justify more RAM if the device supports it. A storage bottleneck may improve with an SSD. Check compatibility and back up your data before hardware work.
author: Tech Compass

title: Bluetooth won’t connect? Start here.
keywords: headphones earbuds wireless pairing bluetooth phone tablet
answer: Charge the accessory, put it into pairing mode, and check whether it is already connected to another device. Bluetooth being switched on is not the same as being discoverable.
sections: 1. Check power and distance
Charge both devices and place them close together. Follow the accessory manual to enter pairing mode; the usual power button action may only turn it on.
2. Check existing connections
Headphones may reconnect automatically to a nearby phone. Disconnect them there, then try pairing with the intended device. Some accessories support multiple connections; others do not.
3. Pair again

In Bluetooth settings, remove the failed pairing only if you know how to pair the accessory again. Restart the accessory and add it as a new device. On Windows, use Settings → Bluetooth & devices; on a phone, open its Bluetooth settings.
Still not connecting?

Test with another compatible device. If the accessory works elsewhere, check the original device’s supported updates and Bluetooth troubleshooting. Use your manufacturer’s drivers rather than third-party driver-download tools.
author: Tech Compass

title: What to do when a computer won’t start
keywords: pc power black screen boot dead laptop turn on
answer: Separate a power problem from a display or startup problem. Check for indicator lights, fan noise, and anything on the screen before deciding what to try.
sections: 1. Check the power path

Use a known-working outlet and the correct manufacturer-approved charger or power cable. Check that plugs are fully seated. Do not use a damaged cable. For a desktop, check the power-supply switch if it has one.
2. Check the display
If lights or fans come on, make sure the monitor has power and the correct input selected. Reseat the display cable with the devices powered off. On a laptop, increase screen brightness.
3. Remove optional accessories
With the computer off, disconnect external drives, docks, and unnecessary USB accessories. Try starting with only essential connections. If it starts, reconnect one accessory at a time.
4. Record what you see

A manufacturer logo, repeated beeps, or a blinking-light pattern can help support identify the next step. Consult the exact device manual. If the operating system offers recovery options, avoid reset or erase choices until your data is backed up.
Know when to stop

Unplug a device that smells burnt or shows damage. Do not open a power supply or attempt to repair a swollen battery. Seek qualified service. This guide cannot diagnose a physical hardware fault remotely.
author: Tech Compass

title: What does a CPU actually do?
keywords: processor central processing unit cores clock
answer: The CPU executes the instructions that make software work. It handles calculations, decisions, and coordination across the computer.
sections: An everyday example

When you open a spreadsheet, the CPU runs the program’s instructions and calculates formulas. The storage supplies the saved file, RAM holds active data, and graphics hardware helps display the result.
Cores and clock speed

A core can execute a stream of instructions. Multiple cores allow more work to happen at once when software can divide its tasks. Clock speed describes cycles per second, but architecture and workload matter too. A higher clock number alone does not prove one processor is faster.
CPU or GPU?

A CPU handles a broad range of tasks. A GPU is particularly suited to many similar calculations in parallel, such as drawing an image. They work together; one is not a universal replacement for the other.
author: Tech Compass

title: What is a GPU?
keywords: graphics card video gaming fps gpu
answer: A GPU is a processor designed to perform many calculations in parallel. It creates graphics for your screen and can also accelerate suitable computing tasks.
sections: Integrated and dedicated graphics

Integrated graphics share the processor package or system design and commonly use system memory. A dedicated graphics card has its own processor and typically its own video memory. Not every computer needs a separate card.
Why games use a GPU

A game needs to draw many pixels, surfaces, and lighting effects repeatedly. GPUs are designed for this parallel work. Frame rate also depends on the CPU, game engine, settings, and display resolution.
Before an upgrade

Check power requirements, case clearance, motherboard connections, and monitor ports. For laptops, the graphics hardware is usually not replaceable. Compare performance in the actual software you use.
author: Tech Compass

title: What is a motherboard?
answer: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the processor, memory, storage, and other components. Its connections determine which parts can work together.
sections: The connections that matter

A motherboard provides a CPU socket, memory slots, storage connections, and expansion slots. It also connects the case’s buttons and ports. The manual explains the location and limits of each connector.
Compatibility comes first

A matching CPU socket is necessary but may not be enough: firmware and chipset support matter too. Check the board manufacturer’s CPU support list and memory specifications. Case size and mounting points also need to match.
When you need the manual
Use the manual for memory slot order, front-panel wiring, and storage installation. Never force a connector. Turn off and unplug the computer before working inside it.
author: Tech Compass

title: SSD vs. HDD: what’s the difference?
keywords: storage disk solid state hard drive nvme sata
answer: An SSD stores data in flash memory. An HDD stores it on spinning magnetic platters. Both keep files without power, but SSDs usually access data much faster.
sections: What you notice in daily use
An SSD usually reduces the wait when starting a computer, opening apps, or loading files. It does not automatically speed up every calculation or solve an internet connection problem.
Capacity and compatibility

Choose a drive that fits the device’s interface and physical space. M.2 describes a form factor; it does not by itself guarantee which storage protocol is supported. Consult the device manual before buying.
Neither is a backup

Either type can fail. Keep a separate copy of important files and check that you can restore them. Before replacing a system drive, plan how you will transfer your files and reinstall or migrate the operating system.
author: Tech Compass

title: Your first PC build: a practical roadmap
keywords: build gaming computer assemble upgrade pc parts
answer: Start with the work you need the computer to do, then choose compatible parts. Build from the component manuals, check each connection, and leave software installation until the hardware passes its first startup.
sections: 1. Plan the whole system

List your software requirements and budget. You will need a compatible CPU, motherboard, memory, storage, power supply, case, and cooling. Add a graphics card when your workload requires one or the processor lacks suitable integrated graphics.
2. Check every fit

Confirm the motherboard supports the CPU and its required firmware. Check memory generation, cooler mounting, case dimensions, GPU clearance, and power connectors. A parts list is not complete until these constraints agree.
3. Prepare a safe workspace

Work on a clean, dry, non-carpeted surface. Follow anti-static precautions in your component manuals. Keep power disconnected while assembling. Never open the power supply or reuse modular power cables from another supply unless the manufacturer confirms compatibility.
4. Assemble using the manuals

Fit the CPU without force, install memory in the recommended slots, and install storage. Fit the cooler following its thermal-paste instructions. Mount the board on the correct case standoffs. Connect the power supply, case controls, fans, and graphics card as required.
5. Check before first power

Check that no loose screws remain, all required power connectors are seated, and fans can rotate freely. Connect a display to the correct graphics output. On first startup, enter firmware setup and check that the expected memory and storage are detected.
6. Install and verify

Install a supported operating system from its official installation media, then updates and manufacturer drivers. Test normal workloads and monitor for stability. If the system fails to start, power off and use the motherboard’s documented diagnostic indicators.
author: Tech Compass

title: What is an operating system?
keywords: os windows macos android ios software applications
answer: An operating system manages a device’s hardware and gives applications a common set of services. Windows, macOS, Linux distributions, Android, and iOS are familiar examples.
sections: What it does for you
The operating system manages memory, files, devices, and running programs. It provides the interface you use to open apps and change settings, plus permissions that control what programs can access.
Why apps need the right version

Apps are built for particular operating systems and hardware. An app for one system will not necessarily run on another. Check the developer’s system requirements and obtain installers from the official source.
Keep it supported

Security updates repair known weaknesses. Check the vendor’s support information for your version. Before a major upgrade, back up important data and check that your essential apps and devices remain compatible.
author: Tech Compass

title: What is Linux?
keywords: linux ubuntu install open source distribution
answer: Linux is the kernel at the center of many operating systems. A Linux distribution, such as Ubuntu, combines that kernel with system tools, applications, and an installer.
sections: Why distributions differ

Distributions choose different desktop interfaces, software packages, release schedules, and support policies. The kernel is only one part of the experience. Choose a distribution with documentation that matches your needs.
Try before replacing your system

Some distributions offer a live USB environment that lets you try the desktop without installing it. Creating that USB erases the selected USB drive. Carefully check the destination and follow the distribution’s official instructions.
Before installation

Back up your files and confirm that you can restore them. Save disk-encryption recovery keys and check hardware compatibility. Installer options that erase or repartition a disk can destroy existing data. Follow the current official guide for the specific release instead of guessing.
Learning the basics

Start with the graphical settings and software manager. Learn how updates work and where your personal files live. Do not run unfamiliar terminal commands with administrator privileges just because a forum post suggests them.
author: Tech Compass

title: What a VPN does—and doesn’t do
keywords: vpn privacy virtual private network encryption anonymous
answer: A VPN creates an encrypted connection between your device and a VPN endpoint. It changes who handles part of your network traffic; it does not make you anonymous or protect you from every online threat.
sections: Where the tunnel ends

A remote-access VPN can connect you to a workplace network. A consumer VPN typically routes internet traffic through a provider. Encryption supplied by the VPN covers the tunnel; HTTPS remains important for the connection to a website.
Who you are trusting

Your VPN provider takes a position of trust in the traffic path. Websites can still identify you through accounts, cookies, and other signals. A VPN does not stop a phishing page from asking for your password.
When troubleshooting

A VPN can affect access to local devices or some websites. If you control the VPN, disconnect briefly on a trusted network to isolate a connection issue. For a work-managed device, ask your IT team before changing required security settings.
author: Tech Compass

title: A calmer approach to computer security
keywords: cybersecurity privacy phishing password malware virus secure learn
answer: Start with supported software, automatic updates, unique passwords, multifactor authentication, and recoverable backups. These habits address common risks without adding a pile of security utilities.
sections: Keep software updated

Enable automatic updates for your operating system, browser, and essential apps. Restart when an update needs it. Remove software you no longer use and replace versions that no longer receive security fixes.
Protect your accounts

Use a reputable password manager to create a different password for every account. Enable multifactor authentication where available; passkeys or security keys can provide phishing-resistant sign-in when supported. Keep recovery codes somewhere safe.
Pause before responding

Unexpected urgency, payment requests, and sign-in links deserve scrutiny. Open the service directly instead of following a suspicious link. Verify unusual requests through a separate, known communication channel.
Back up and test recovery

Keep a separate backup of important data. Make sure at least one copy is protected from accidental deletion or ransomware affecting your main device. Periodically restore a sample file to check that recovery works.
If you suspect a compromise

Use another trusted device to change affected account passwords and review account sessions. Contact your organization’s IT team for managed equipment. Avoid installing unfamiliar cleanup tools or paying someone who contacted you unexpectedly.
author: Tech Compass

title: iPhone or iPad won’t connect to Wi-Fi
keywords: iphone ipad ios ipados apple wifi wireless internet phone tablet
answer: Check Settings → Wi-Fi first. A checkmark beside a network means you joined it, but does not guarantee internet access. Compare with another device on the same network.
sections: 1. Confirm the connection
Open Settings → Wi-Fi, turn Wi-Fi on, and select your network. Check the password carefully. Move within range of the router.
2. Restart and compare
Restart your iPhone or iPad. If other devices also cannot connect, restart the router when it is safe to interrupt the household connection. Test again.
3. Try another network
If the device works on another trusted Wi-Fi network, investigate the original router or internet service. If it cannot connect anywhere, contact Apple Support.
Before resetting network settings

A network reset removes saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords and resets cellular, VPN, and APN settings. Keep this as a later step, following Apple’s current instructions. Ask your administrator first on a managed device.
author: Tech Compass

title: Google Nest speaker won’t connect to Wi-Fi
keywords: google nest home smart speaker display wifi wireless setup connect offline
answer: Check power, network credentials, and distance from the router before changing router settings. These checks apply to Google Nest and Home speakers and displays, not every smart-home product.
sections: 1. Check setup conditions
Keep the speaker or display near the router during setup. Confirm the phone running Google Home is connected to the intended network and that you have the right password.
2. Restart before resetting
Restart the speaker or display, then try setup again in Google Home. If other devices have connection trouble too, restart the router after warning anyone using it.
3. Test the other band
With a dual-band router, try the other supported band: 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz. Do not assume every smart device supports both. Follow the instructions for your specific model.
If setup still fails
Record the error shown in Google Home and consult Google’s troubleshooting page. Avoid a factory reset until you have reviewed its effects and are ready to set the device up again.
author: Tech Compass
